text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Soldiers in the Democratic Republic of Congo are barring Zambian women wearing trousers from entering the country. They say they will not allow women to dress like men.
- The agriculture ministry says the African Development Bank has released $100 million towards Zambia's rural investment scheme.
- The opposition United National Independence Party (UNIP) refutes government allegations that former president Kenneth Kaunda is training mercenaries to dislodge the government from power.
- Germany approves a $5,4 million grant for a teak forest project.
- Defence minister Ben Mwila says Zambia is a de facto one party state, largely because the opposition is disorganised.
- A former legal affairs minister in the ousted Hutu-dominated Rwandese government Agness Ntangibyaliro Rutugwera has been abducted from the northern town of Mufulira.
- The truckers association says a 24 percent fuel price rise effected early this month has pushed Zambian transporters out of regional competition.
